spots.name: Jardim do Torel
spots.neighborhood: Colina de Santana / Avenida da Liberdade
spots.blurb: A small terraced garden on a hill above Avenida da Liberdade, with benches under mature trees and a low wall to lean on while looking across the rooftops toward Bairro Alto. It draws neighbours with books and dogs rather than tour groups, so you can sit for an hour without anyone moving you along.
spots.tips: Ride the Lavra funicular from Largo da Anunciada, then walk two minutes uphill; the benches on the lower terrace catch the late-afternoon light. Some summers the council turns the pond area into a temporary 'beach' and it gets busier.

safety.note: Residential hill, quiet in the evening; the funicular stops running in the evening (around 8pm), so plan the walk down.

spots.verifyNote: Well-known public garden, kept from reviewer knowledge; no search confirmation possible this session. Softened the summer 'beach' claim and the funicular closing time.

spots.name: Tapada das Necessidades
spots.blurb: A walled former royal park behind the Necessidades Palace, with a cactus garden, an old greenhouse, a pond and sloping lawns that look south over the river toward the 25 de Abril bridge. It is big enough to lose yourself in and mostly used by neighbours walking dogs or lying on the grass, making it one of the easiest places in central Lisbon to be alone.
spots.tips: Enter from Largo das Necessidades (tram 25 or bus 727) and head uphill past the cactus garden for the lawn with the bridge view. There is no cafe inside, so bring water and snacks; gates close in the evening.

safety.note: Gated park, daytime only; some upper corners are secluded, so stick to the main lawns if alone.

spots.verifyNote: Long-established public park, kept from reviewer knowledge. Wikipedia title from reviewer knowledge, not search-confirmed (a GitHub probe found only the Portuguese article); set to null if the English page does not resolve. Removed the peacocks claim.

spots.name: Jardim da Cerca da Graça
spots.blurb: A wide sloping lawn on the old grounds of the Graça convent, opened as a public park in 2015 and still mostly a neighbourhood thing. Locals spread blankets in the evening for the view across Mouraria to the castle, and a small kiosk, an orchard and a playground make it feel lived-in without ever being packed.
spots.tips: Enter from Calçada do Monte or Rua da Senhora da Glória; the upper lawn near the kiosk faces the sunset. Kiosk hours are irregular, so bring your own drinks if you are counting on one.

safety.note: Gated with posted hours; lit paths, but it empties quickly after dark.

spots.verifyNote: Municipal park opened 2015, kept from reviewer knowledge; no search confirmation possible this session.

spots.name: Miradouro do Monte Agudo
spots.blurb: A small neighbourhood miradouro at the top of Penha de França with a wooden deck, a few benches and a kiosk, looking over the eastern rooftops to the river and the Vasco da Gama bridge. It rarely makes the guidebooks, so evenings are mostly residents with a drink watching the light change.
spots.tips: Walk up Rua Heliodoro Salgado from Anjos or Arroios (about 15 minutes uphill); the deck fills at sunset on warm weekends, so come 30 minutes early for a bench.

safety.note: Lit, residential street with a kiosk open into the evening; quiet but not isolated.

spots.verifyNote: Small municipal viewpoint, kept from reviewer knowledge; no search confirmation possible this session. Moved the safety claim out of tips.

spots.name: Ribeira das Naus
spots.blurb: A stepped riverside promenade between Cais do Sodré and Praça do Comércio where the old shipyard was turned into a lawn and wide stone steps down to the water. At golden hour locals sit on the steps with a drink from the kiosk and watch the ferries cross to Cacilhas; it is central but spreads people out enough to feel unhurried.
spots.tips: The steps nearest Cais do Sodré catch the last sun; bring a jacket because the river breeze picks up after sunset. Cais das Colunas, a few minutes east, is a quieter place to sit right at the water's edge.

safety.note: Busy and lit into the night, but pickpockets and persistent street hawkers work the Cais do Sodré end after dark; keep bags zipped, sit near the kiosk rather than the darker far steps late, and take a ride-hail rather than a long walk if leaving after midnight.

spots.verifyNote: Central public promenade, kept from reviewer knowledge. Level set to caution because of well-known late-night petty theft and hawker hassle around Cais do Sodré.

spots.name: Passeio do Tejo (Parque das Nações)
spots.blurb: A long, flat riverfront promenade built for Expo 98, running past the Garcia de Orta gardens, the cable car and the Vasco da Gama tower with the bridge stretching across the estuary. It faces east, so this is Lisbon's easiest sunrise spot, and the wide paths, lawns and benches stay well-lit and used by joggers and families into the evening.
spots.tips: Start at Oriente station and walk north along the water toward the Vasco da Gama tower for the widest views and fewest people. Mornings are almost empty; on weekend afternoons the stretch by the Oceanário gets busy.

safety.note: Modern, well-lit promenade with steady foot traffic; fine solo in the evening, quieter north of the tower late.

spots.verifyNote: Expo 98 riverfront, kept from reviewer knowledge. Removed the 'police presence' claim. The district article 'Parque das Nações' is not about the promenade itself, so wikipediaTitle stays null.

spots.name: Jardim do Campo Grande
spots.blurb: A long, leafy park in the north of the city with a lake, sports courts, cafes and plenty of shaded lawn, used mostly by students from the nearby university and local families. It is far enough from the tourist centre that you can nap under a tree or read on a bench by the water without any miradouro crowds.
spots.tips: The southern half near the lake has the best shade and a cafe with tables; metro Campo Grande drops you at the top end. Paths are lit and busy in the evening but thin out late.

safety.note: Large open park that empties after about 11pm and has unlit stretches along its length; late at night stay in the southern half by the cafes and the lit main-avenue paths, or treat it as a daytime spot.

spots.verifyNote: Major municipal park, kept from reviewer knowledge. Removed 'rowing boats' and 'tennis courts' (unverified after the park's refurbishment). Level set to caution for late-night use of a large 24h park.

spots.name: Jardim Gulbenkian
spots.blurb: The modernist garden around the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, with a duck pond, winding paths, an open-air amphitheatre and lawns tucked among concrete and greenery. Office workers and students come here to eat lunch, read or nap on the grass, and the garden is free even though the museums beside it are not.
spots.tips: Enter from Avenida de Berna or Rua Marquês de Fronteira; the lawn by the lake near the amphitheatre is the classic spot. Gates close in the early evening, so treat it as a daytime place.
spots.hours: daily, roughly 10am-6pm, later in summer (check site)
spots.verifyNote: Well-known free garden, kept from reviewer knowledge. The 'Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation' article is about the institution, not the garden, so wikipediaTitle stays null.

spots.name: Biblioteca Palácio Galveias
spots.blurb: A municipal public library in an 18th-century palace beside Campo Pequeno, with high-ceilinged reading rooms and a quiet garden. Anyone can walk in and sit with a book or laptop for the afternoon at no cost, and the rooms stay calm even when the square outside is busy.
spots.tips: Bring a laptop or a book; there is wifi and desks in the reading rooms, and the garden benches are good on warm days. Check the Lisbon libraries site for current hours before going on a Saturday.

safety.note: Staffed public building in a busy area.

spots.verifyNote: Municipal library (reopened after renovation in 2017), kept from reviewer knowledge. Removed the cafe mention and the specific closing time, both unverified.

spots.name: Ler Devagar
spots.blurb: A former printing works turned multi-storey bookshop inside LX Factory, with iron walkways, a suspended flying bicycle and a cafe-bar on the ground floor. It gets photographed a lot, but on weekday afternoons you can climb to the upper galleries, find a stool among the shelves and read undisturbed.
spots.tips: Avoid Sunday, when the LX Factory market fills the whole complex; late weekday afternoons are quiet. The cafe serves drinks you can carry up to the mezzanine tables.
spots.hours: daily from around noon, later on Fri-Sat (check site)

sources.label: awesome-hacking-locations: community list of laptop-friendly places, includes Ler Devagar

safety.note: Inside a busy, lit complex with restaurants open late.

spots.verifyNote: Long-running bookshop in LX Factory, kept from reviewer knowledge; the one source is a GitHub README that appeared in a code-search result. Wikipedia title from reviewer knowledge, not search-confirmed; set to null if the page does not resolve.

spots.name: Terraços do Centro Cultural de Belém
spots.blurb: The public terraces and olive garden on top of the Centro Cultural de Belém, a stone-and-water landscape that looks straight over the river to the Discoveries monument and the bridge. It is free to walk up to and largely ignored by the crowds queuing at the monastery, so you get the Belém views with almost nobody around, plus a cafe on the upper level.
spots.tips: Enter from Praça do Império and take the stairs or ramps up to the Jardim das Oliveiras; the west-facing edge is best at sunset. Bring a windbreaker, the terrace is exposed.
spots.hours: daily daytime, closes in the evening (check site)

safety.note: Staffed cultural centre; terraces close in the evening.

spots.verifyNote: Major public cultural centre; the terraces are part of the building the article describes, so the title is kept with high confidence.

spots.name: Praça das Flores
spots.blurb: A small tree-shaded square between São Bento and Príncipe Real with a fountain, benches, a kiosk and a couple of cafes on its edges. It is a neighbourhood square rather than a destination, so afternoons are dog walkers, kids and people with a coffee and the newspaper, and evenings are locals at the kiosk tables.
spots.tips: The kiosk does coffee and drinks into the evening; the benches on the north side keep the shade. It is a ten-minute walk from Rato or Chiado.

safety.note: Lit residential square with cafes open into the evening.

spots.verifyNote: Neighbourhood square, kept from reviewer knowledge; no search confirmation possible this session.

spots.name: Praia de Paço de Arcos
spots.blurb: A small town beach on the Oeiras coast, about 20 minutes by train from Cais do Sodré, with a promenade, a leafy seafront garden and a sheltered bay. It is where people from the western suburbs go for an evening walk or a swim after work, so it stays relaxed even in summer while Carcavelos next door fills up.
spots.tips: Get off at Paço de Arcos station and walk down through the village to the sand; the Passeio Marítimo lets you keep walking west to Oeiras or east toward Caxias at sunset. There are cafes along the seafront garden, but the beach itself has no facilities outside the summer season.

safety.note: Lit promenade and Cascais-line trains until late; the sand itself is dark after sunset, so stay on the promenade if lingering.

spots.verifyNote: Town beach in Oeiras (about 14 km from the centre), kept from reviewer knowledge. Softened the fishing-boats and cafe-closing claims. The 'Paço de Arcos' article is about the town, not the beach, so wikipediaTitle stays null.
